_about: Creation told again (plan 7.6b): things the creation accounts and the places that retell them say in shared words, from Genesis and the Psalms to John, the letters and Revelation, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi. Psalms & elsewhere: any other Old Testament book.

rows.title: In the beginning

Genesis: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth
The Prophets: Has it not been declared to you from the beginning?
Psalms & elsewhere: In the beginning You laid the foundations of the earth
From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began
Gospels & Acts: In the beginning was the Word
He was with God in the beginning
from the beginning of God's creation until now
The letters: In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth
everything continues as it has from the beginning of creation
Revelation: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End
the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End

rows.alike: Genesis 1:1, John 1:1, Psalm 102:25 and Hebrews 1:10 each open with "In the beginning"; Mark 10:6 and 2 Peter 3:4 both say "from the beginning of creation".
rows.different: What stands at the beginning differs: in Genesis "God created the heavens and the earth"; in John "was the Word"; in Psalm 102 and Hebrews 1 "You laid the foundations of the earth"; in Proverbs 8 the speaker says "I was established, from the beginning". In Revelation "the Beginning and the End" is said in the first person: "I am the Alpha and the Omega".

rows.title: The Maker of heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them

Genesis: God created the heavens and the earth
the heavens and the earth when they were created
The Prophets: You made the heavens and the earth
You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and outstretched arm
He who created the heavens and stretched them out
Psalms & elsewhere: the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them
the LORD made the heavens and the earth
You made the heavens and the earth
who made the heavens and the earth
You created the heavens, the highest heavens with all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them
the Maker of heaven and earth
the Maker of heaven and earth
the Maker of heaven and earth
the Maker of heaven and earth
the Maker of heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them
the LORD who made the heavens
the LORD who made the heavens
Gospels & Acts: You made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them
who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them
The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth
Revelation: who created heaven and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it
Worship the One who made the heavens and the earth and the sea and the springs of waters

rows.alike: Genesis 1:1 says "God created the heavens and the earth", and the same pair recurs in prayer and praise: "You made the heavens and the earth" (2 Kings 19:15, Isaiah 37:16), "the Maker of heaven and earth" (Psalms 115 to 146). Exodus 20:11, Nehemiah 9:6, Psalm 146:6, Acts 4:24 and 14:15 and Revelation 10:6 add "the sea" and all that is in them. 1 Chronicles 16:26 and Psalm 96:5 say "the LORD who made the heavens", Psalm 136:5 says "He made the heavens", and Isaiah 42:5 has "He who created the heavens".
rows.different: Exodus 20:11 and 31:17 say "in six days"; Nehemiah 9:6 has "the highest heavens with all their host"; Jeremiah 32:17 has "by Your great power and outstretched arm"; Acts 17:24 has "the world and everything in it"; Revelation 14:7 ends with "the springs of waters". In Genesis 14:19 "Creator of heaven and earth" is spoken in a blessing of Abram, and in 14:22 by Abram to the king of Sodom.

rows.title: By His word, at His command

Genesis: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light
The Prophets: when I summon them, they stand up together
Psalms & elsewhere: By the word of the LORD the heavens were made
For He spoke, and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm
He gave the command and they were created
Gospels & Acts: In the beginning was the Word
Through Him all things were made
The letters: the universe was formed at God's command
by God's word the heavens existed and the earth was formed out of water and by water
upholding all things by His powerful word
Revelation: by Your will they exist and were created

rows.alike: Genesis 1 repeats "And God said" and "And it was so"; Psalm 33 says "By the word of the LORD the heavens were made" and "He spoke, and it came to be"; Psalm 148:5 "He gave the command and they were created"; Hebrews 11:3 "formed at God's command"; 2 Peter 3:5 "by God's word the heavens existed".
rows.different: Genesis gives the words spoken ("Let there be light"); the Psalms and the letters report that He spoke or commanded. John speaks of "the Word" through whom "all things were made"; Hebrews 11:3 adds "what is seen was not made out of what was visible"; 2 Peter adds "out of water and by water"; Hebrews 1:3 speaks of the Son "upholding all things by His powerful word"; Revelation 4:11 says "by Your will".

rows.title: The Spirit of God and the breath of life

Genesis: the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters
everything that has the breath of life in it
breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being
every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life
every creature with the breath of life
everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died
The Prophets: who gives breath to the people on it and life to those who walk in it
the breath of life I have made
who forms the spirit of man within him
Psalms & elsewhere: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life
all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust
By His breath the skies were cleared
all the stars by the breath of His mouth
when You take away their breath, they die and return to dust
When You send Your Spirit, they are created
the spirit returns to God who gave it
the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding
Gospels & Acts: He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else
Revelation: the breath of life from God entered the two witnesses

rows.alike: Genesis 1:2 has "the Spirit of God" over the waters and Genesis 2:7 has God breathe "the breath of life" into the man; Job 33:4 has both words together, "The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life", and Psalm 104:30 says "When You send Your Spirit, they are created".
rows.different: Genesis 2:7 tells of one man breathed into; Isaiah 42:5 and Acts 17:25 speak of God who "gives breath" to all people. Psalm 104:29 and Job 34:14-15 tell of breath withdrawn and a return "to dust". Psalm 33:6 and Job 26:13 speak of God's own breath: "the breath of His mouth", "By His breath the skies were cleared".

rows.title: Light out of darkness

Genesis: “Let there be light,” and there was light
He separated the light from the darkness
The Prophets: I form the light and create the darkness
Psalms & elsewhere: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides
at the boundary between light and darkness
He wraps Himself in light as with a garment
You bring darkness, and it becomes night
Gospels & Acts: that life was the light of men
The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it
The letters: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts

rows.alike: Genesis 1:3-4 has "Let there be light" and God "separated the light from the darkness"; Isaiah 45:7 "I form the light and create the darkness"; John 1:5 "The Light shines in the darkness"; 2 Corinthians 4:6 "God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,”".
rows.different: In Genesis God speaks the light and divides it from the darkness; in Isaiah 45:7 God says He forms the one and creates the other. John speaks of "the Light" and says "that life was the light of men"; 2 Corinthians 4:6 goes on to God's light shining "in our hearts". Psalm 104:2 says He "wraps Himself in light as with a garment"; Job 38:19 asks "Where is the way to the home of light?"

rows.title: Lights to rule the day and the night

Genesis: Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night
let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years
the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night
The Prophets: who gives the sun for light by day, who sets in order the moon and stars for light by night
No longer will the sun be your light by day, nor the brightness of the moon shine on your night
Psalms & elsewhere: the sun to rule the day
the moon and stars to govern the night
He made the moon to mark the seasons; the sun knows when to set
The day is Yours, and also the night; You established the moon and the sun
Revelation: the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it
they will have no need for the light of a lamp or of the sun

rows.alike: Genesis 1:16 has "the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night" and Psalm 136 "the sun to rule the day ... the moon and stars to govern the night"; Jeremiah 31:35 "the sun for light by day ... the moon and stars for light by night". Genesis 1:14 has the lights as "signs to mark the seasons", and Psalm 104:19 says He made the moon "to mark the seasons".
rows.different: Genesis does not name the sun and moon, calling them "the greater light" and "the lesser light"; the Psalms and Jeremiah name them. Isaiah 60:19 and Revelation 21:23 speak of no need of sun or moon, and Revelation 22:5 of no need of "the light of a lamp or of the sun", because "the LORD will be your everlasting light", "the glory of God illuminates the city" and "the Lord God will shine on them".

rows.title: He made the stars, numbered and named

Genesis: And He made the stars as well
The Prophets: Who created all these? He leads forth the starry host by number; He calls each one by name
He who made the Pleiades and Orion
Psalms & elsewhere: He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name
all the stars by the breath of His mouth
the moon and the stars, which You have set in place
He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades
while the morning stars sang together
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?

rows.alike: Genesis 1:16 says "He made the stars as well"; Psalm 147:4 "He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name" and Isaiah 40:26 "He leads forth the starry host by number; He calls each one by name"; Job 9:9 and Amos 5:8 name "the Pleiades" and "Orion" as His making.
rows.different: Genesis gives the stars one clause after the two great lights; Isaiah 40:26 puts it as a question, "Who created all these?". Job 38:31 asks "Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades", and Job 38:7 has "the morning stars sang together"; Psalm 33:6 says all the stars were made "by the breath of His mouth".

rows.title: He stretched out the heavens and spread out the earth

The Prophets: He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in
He who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and its offspring
who alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth
It was My hands that stretched out the heavens
My right hand spread out the heavens
stretched out the heavens by His understanding
stretched out the heavens by His understanding
Psalms & elsewhere: He stretches out the heavens like a tent
He alone stretches out the heavens
He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth upon nothing
He spread out the earth upon the waters

rows.alike: Psalm 104:2 and Isaiah 40:22 both say He "stretches out the heavens" "like a tent"; the same words recur through Isaiah, Jeremiah, Zechariah and Job. Isaiah 42:5 and 44:24 and Psalm 136:6 add that He "spread out the earth".
rows.different: Job 9:8 and Isaiah 44:24 say "alone"; Isaiah 40:22 adds "like a curtain"; Isaiah 45:12 and 48:13 speak of "My hands" and "My right hand"; Jeremiah says "by His understanding"; Psalm 136:6 says "upon the waters" and Job 26:7 "He hangs the earth upon nothing". Job 37:18 puts it as a question: "can you, like Him, spread out the skies".

rows.title: The foundations of the earth

The Prophets: Surely My own hand founded the earth
laid the foundations of the earth
lays the foundation of the earth
Have you not understood since the foundation of the earth?
Psalms & elsewhere: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?
On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone
You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands
He set the earth on its foundations, never to be moved
For He has founded it upon the seas and established it upon the waters
The earth and its fullness You founded
The LORD founded the earth by wisdom
when He marked out the foundations of the earth
The letters: You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands

rows.alike: Job 38:4, Psalm 102:25, Isaiah 51:13 and Hebrews 1:10 all say God "laid the foundations of the earth", and Zechariah 12:1 says He "lays the foundation of the earth"; Psalm 104:5, Psalm 24:2, Psalm 89:11, Proverbs 3:19 and Isaiah 48:13 say He set or "founded" it.
rows.different: In Job 38 God asks Job "Where were you" and "who laid its cornerstone"; Psalm 24:2 says "upon the seas"; Psalm 104:5 says "never to be moved"; Proverbs 3:19 says "by wisdom". Hebrews 1:10 reads as Psalm 102:25 does, with "O Lord" after "In the beginning".

rows.title: Who measured it? Who was His counselor?

The Prophets: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his hand?
Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or informed Him as His counselor?
Whom did He consult to enlighten Him
Psalms & elsewhere: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
Tell Me, if you have understanding
Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth?
The letters: Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?

rows.alike: Job 38, Isaiah 40 and Proverbs 30 tell the making as a string of questions beginning "Who": "Who fixed its measurements?", "Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand", "Who has bound up the waters in His cloak?". Isaiah 40:13 and Romans 11:34 both ask who has been "His counselor".
rows.different: In Job God speaks in the first person ("Tell Me, if you have understanding") and asks Job ("Surely you know!"); Isaiah 40:12 speaks of "his hand" and Proverbs 30:4 of "His hands" and "His cloak". Romans 11:34 asks only of "the mind of the Lord" and His counselor, not of measuring.

rows.title: A boundary for the sea

Genesis: Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear
the gathering of waters He called “seas.”
The Prophets: the One who set the sand as the boundary for the sea, an enduring barrier it cannot cross
who made the sea and the dry land
Psalms & elsewhere: He piles up the waters of the sea; He puts the depths into storehouses
At Your rebuke the waters fled
to the place You assigned for them
You set a boundary they cannot cross, that they may never again cover the earth
Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb
when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors
You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop
when He set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command
The sea is His, for He made it, and His hands formed the dry land
You set all the boundaries of the earth

rows.alike: Psalm 104:9 says "You set a boundary they cannot cross", Proverbs 8:29 "He set a boundary for the sea", Jeremiah 5:22 "set the sand as the boundary for the sea" and Job 38:10 "I fixed its boundaries"; Genesis 1:9 has the waters "gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear", and Psalm 104:8 sends them "to the place You assigned for them". Jonah 1:9 says the LORD "made the sea and the dry land", and Psalm 95:5 that "His hands formed the dry land".
rows.different: Genesis tells it as a command ("Let the waters ... be gathered"); Psalm 104:7 says the waters "fled" "At Your rebuke"; in Job 38 the sea "burst forth from the womb" and God speaks to it: "You may come this far, but no farther". Jeremiah names the boundary as "the sand"; Proverbs 8:29 adds "so that the waters would not surpass His command".

rows.title: The surface of the deep

Genesis: Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep
The Prophets: He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth
I looked at the earth, and it was formless and void; I looked to the heavens, and they had no light
Psalms & elsewhere: You covered it with the deep like a garment; the waters stood above the mountains
When there were no watery depths, I was brought forth
when He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep
when the fountains of the deep gushed forth
He has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters
walked in the trenches of the deep
the surface of the deep is frozen
The letters: the earth was formed out of water and by water

rows.alike: Genesis 1:2 says "darkness was over the surface of the deep"; Proverbs 8:27 has "a circle on the face of the deep" and Job 26:10 "a horizon on the face of the waters"; Psalm 104:6 says "You covered it with the deep like a garment".
rows.different: Genesis says the earth "was formless and void"; Proverbs 8:27 and Job 26:10 say He "inscribed" a circle or a horizon on the water, and Isaiah 40:22 speaks of "the circle of the earth". 2 Peter 3:5 says the earth "was formed out of water and by water". Jeremiah 4:23 has the words "formless and void" of what he saw when "I looked at the earth".

rows.title: God saw that it was good

Genesis: And God saw that the light was good
And God saw that it was good
And God saw that it was good
And God saw that it was good
And God saw that it was good
And God saw that it was good
And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good
It is not good for the man to be alone
The letters: For every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected

rows.alike: Genesis 1 says six times "God saw that it was good" and at the end "it was very good"; 1 Timothy 4:4 says "every creation of God is good".
rows.different: In Genesis it is God who sees that it is good; 1 Timothy 4:4 says "every creation of God is good" and adds "nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected". Genesis 2:18 has God say "It is not good for the man to be alone".

rows.title: The sea creatures and the beasts of the earth

Genesis: Let the waters teem with living creatures
So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves
Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds
God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds
Psalms & elsewhere: the earth is full of Your creatures
Here is the sea, vast and wide, teeming with creatures beyond number, living things both great and small
There the ships pass, and Leviathan, which You formed to frolic there
all great sea creatures and ocean depths
wild animals and all cattle, crawling creatures and flying birds

rows.alike: Genesis 1:20 has "Let the waters teem with living creatures" and Psalm 104:25 "the sea ... teeming with creatures beyond number"; Genesis 1:21 and Psalm 148:7 both name "great sea creatures"; Genesis 1:24 and Psalm 148:10 list cattle or livestock, crawling creatures and wild beasts.
rows.different: Genesis tells them made "according to their kinds"; Psalm 104:26 names "Leviathan, which You formed to frolic there" alongside "the ships"; Psalm 148 calls them to praise: "Praise the LORD from the earth".

rows.title: Food for every creature

Genesis: I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth
They will be yours for food
I have given every green plant for food
just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you all things
Psalms & elsewhere: He makes the grass grow for the livestock and provides crops for man to cultivate, bringing forth food from the earth
All creatures look to You to give them their food in due season
The eyes of all look to You, and You give them their food in season
He provides food for the animals, and for the young ravens when they call
Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God
Gospels & Acts: Look at the birds of the air

rows.alike: Genesis 1:29-30 has "I have given every green plant for food"; Psalm 104:27 and 145:15 "give them their food in due season" and "in season"; Psalm 147:9 and Job 38:41 say He "provides food for" the young ravens; Luke 12:24 "Consider the ravens ... yet God feeds them".
rows.different: Genesis gives the food in God's own words ("I have given"), and Genesis 9:3 has God say "I now give you all things". The Psalms speak to or of God in the present; Job 38:41 is God's question to Job. Matthew 6:26 and Luke 12:24 are said to hearers, with "Are you not much more valuable than they?" and "How much more valuable you are than the birds!".

rows.title: Formed from the dust, a living being

Genesis: the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being
out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air
For dust you are, and to dust you shall return
Psalms & elsewhere: He is mindful that we are dust
they die and return to dust
You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?
mankind would return to the dust
all come from dust, and all return to dust
the dust returns to the ground from which it came
The letters: The first man Adam became a living being
The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven
the last Adam a life-giving spirit
As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth

rows.alike: Genesis 2:7 says "the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground" and 3:19 "For dust you are, and to dust you shall return"; the word "dust" recurs in "we are dust" (Psalm 103:14), "all come from dust, and all return to dust" (Ecclesiastes 3:20) and "The first man was of the dust of the earth" (1 Corinthians 15:47). Genesis 2:7 and 1 Corinthians 15:45 both have "became a living being".
rows.different: Genesis 2:19 says the beasts and birds too were formed "out of the ground"; Job 10:9 says "You molded me like clay". Ecclesiastes 12:7 adds "the spirit returns to God who gave it". 1 Corinthians 15:45 has Genesis 2:7's words "became a living being" and sets beside them "the last Adam a life-giving spirit", and 15:47 "the second man from heaven". 1 Corinthians 15:48 goes on "As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth".

rows.title: Male and female; the two become one flesh

Genesis: male and female He created them
Male and female He created them, and He blessed them
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh
bring two of every living creature into the ark-male and female
seven pairs of every kind of bird of the air, male and female
two by two, male and female
the male and female of every living thing
Gospels & Acts: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate
God made them male and female
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife
and the two will become one flesh
Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate
The letters: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh
The two will become one flesh

rows.alike: Genesis 1:27 says "male and female He created them" and 2:24 "they will become one flesh"; in Matthew 19 and Mark 10 Jesus gives both sayings one after the other, and Ephesians 5:31 gives 2:24 with "the two" where Genesis has "they".
rows.different: Genesis 2:24 reads "they will become one flesh"; Matthew, Mark and Ephesians read "the two will become one flesh". Matthew says "the Creator" where Mark says "God"; both Gospels add "what God has joined together, let man not separate". 1 Corinthians 6:16 uses the words of one who "unites himself with a prostitute".

rows.title: Woman taken from man

Genesis: I will make for him a suitable helper
from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman
This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh
for out of man she was taken
The letters: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man
Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man
For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God
For Adam was formed first, and then Eve

rows.alike: Genesis 2:23 says "out of man she was taken"; 1 Corinthians 11:8 says "woman from man" and 11:12 "woman came from man"; 1 Timothy 2:13 says "Adam was formed first, and then Eve".
rows.different: Genesis tells it as an event, with the rib, and gives the man's words "bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh" and God's "a suitable helper". 1 Corinthians 11:12 adds "so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God". 1 Corinthians 11:8 and 1 Timothy 2:13 each begin with "For".

rows.title: On the seventh day He rested

Genesis: And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work
Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it
Psalms & elsewhere: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested
Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy
for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, but on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed
The letters: And on the seventh day God rested from all His works
His works have been finished since the foundation of the world

rows.alike: Genesis 2:2 says "on that day He rested from all His work"; Exodus 20:11 and 31:17 "on the seventh day He rested"; Hebrews 4:4 "on the seventh day God rested from all His works". Genesis 2:3 "God blessed the seventh day" and Exodus 20:11 "the LORD blessed the Sabbath day".
rows.different: Genesis does not use the word "Sabbath"; Exodus 20:11 follows "on the seventh day He rested" with "Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy", and Exodus 31:17 reads "a sign between Me and the Israelites forever" and adds "and was refreshed". Hebrews 4:3-4 sets the seventh day beside "They shall never enter My rest".

rows.title: All things made, through Him

The Prophets: I am the LORD, who has made all things
Gospels & Acts: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made
the world was made through Him
The letters: For in Him all things were created
All things were created through Him and for Him
He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together
one God, the Father, from whom all things came
one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came
through whom He made the universe
for whom and through whom all things exist
For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things

rows.alike: Isaiah 44:24 says "who has made all things", Ephesians 3:9 "God, who created all things", Revelation 4:11 "You created all things"; John 1:3 says "Through Him all things were made" and Colossians 1:16 "All things were created through Him and for Him".
rows.different: Who is named differs: John 1:3 and 1:10 and Colossians 1:16 say "Through Him" and "in Him" without naming him in these verses; 1 Corinthians 8:6 names "one God, the Father, from whom all things came" and "one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came"; Hebrews 1:2 has "His Son", "through whom He made the universe"; Hebrews 2:10 says "God, for whom and through whom all things exist"; Romans 11:36 says "from Him and through Him and to Him"; Revelation 4:11 is sung to "our Lord and God". Colossians 1:17 adds "in Him all things hold together".

rows.title: By wisdom and understanding

The Prophets: The LORD made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding
The LORD made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding
His understanding is beyond searching out
Psalms & elsewhere: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding
In wisdom You have made them all
By His insight He made the heavens
I was there when He established the heavens
Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side
by His understanding He shattered Rahab

rows.alike: Proverbs 3:19 says "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding", and Jeremiah 10:12 and 51:15 "established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding"; Psalm 104:24 says "In wisdom You have made them all".
rows.different: Jeremiah adds "by His power"; Psalm 136:5 says "By His insight". In Proverbs 8:27 and 8:30 a speaker says "I was there when He established the heavens" and "I was a skilled craftsman at His side".
